newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FACTORY START-UP PROBLEMS DEPRESS TULIP H1.
newsitem.headline: FACTORY START-UP PROBLEMS DEPRESS TULIP H1.

text.p: Personal computer maker Tulip said on Thursday the start-up problems at its new factory which dragged down turnover in the first half had been resolved, putting it on course for higher second-half earnings.
It said double premises costs in the first two months of this year plus extra start-up costs for its new factory had strongly dragged down its first-half result.
The PC manufacturer earlier reported a loss of 6.8 million guilders in the first half of 1997. In the same year-earlier period, Tulip booked a loss of 12.7 million guilders.
Tulip said teething problems at its new factory had led to "significant turnover losses" in the months to end-May.
But it added, "The start-up problems were resolved from June and will no longer have a negative influence on results in the second half of the year."
Gross margins rose to 28.7 percent in the first half from a year-earlier 18.3 percent due to the new factory, it said.
The factory is based on "building to order" rather than "building to inventory", whereby writedowns on inventory have been sharply reduced, Tulip said.
The PC maker is forecasting a year-on-year sales increase in the second half and suggests it could even finish the full year in profit.
"Barring unforeseen circumstances, management...expects that the full 1997 year need not be closed with a negative result," it said.
